key_insight: Adaptive single-copy Clifford measurements can learn any n-qubit stabilizer state with optimal Θ(n) sample complexity, closing the gap to two-copy Bell-measurement methods.
engineering_relevance: This reduces measurement overhead for quantum state characterization, improving practical workflows for error-correction benchmarking, verification, and stabilizer-based simulation.
method: Use adaptive, polynomial-time single-copy Clifford measurements instead of multi-copy Bell measurements.
Exploit measurement choices conditioned on previous outcomes to recover the stabilizer structure efficiently.
Extend the same adaptive strategy to tolerant testing and low-nullity near-stabilizer states.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimal Θ(n) learning with single-copy measurements, a sample-optimal tolerant tester, a Θ(n-k+1/ε) testing tradeoff with k qubits of memory, and O(n2^r) scaling for states of stabilizer nullity at most r.
watch_item: The approach relies on adaptive measurement control and Clifford-capable hardware, so runtime and coherence constraints may limit performance in near-term implementations.
paper_title: Adaptivity is all you need: Optimal stabilizer learning using just single-copy measurements
